headline: Local Magistrate Begins Issuing Summons To Cloud Formations For 'Unauthorized Shadows' Over High-Court Parking Lot
body:
A local district magistrate has initiated a series of formal legal notices directed at various cumulonimbus cloud formations hovering over the city’s High Court complex, citing a clear violation of municipal parking aesthetics and unpermitted light obstruction. The order, delivered via a series of aerial balloons carrying embossed envelopes, mandates that all passing weather systems must appear before the bench to explain their lack of prior clearance to shade the staff’s official vehicles.

"The court has been very clear that nothing, living or meteorological, is allowed to cast a shadow on the judicial premises without a stamped NOC," explained a court clerk who spent most of Tuesday morning attempting to serve a subpoena to a particularly stubborn gust of wind. "The clouds were found in contempt for drifting into the court’s designated sun-exposure zone, which was specifically reserved for the parking of official SUVs. We don't care if it's natural; if it blocks the view of the gate, it requires a written application."

Witnesses report that the magistrate has already threatened to hold the monsoon season in civil detention if the clouds do not vacate the airspace by Friday. While legal experts suggest that weather patterns generally lack the capacity to enter a plea, the magistrate remains undeterred, insisting that ignorance of the law is no excuse for a rainstorm, even one operating at an altitude of ten thousand feet.
caption: Rain or shine, the summons doesn't care. The weather is officially under investigation for unauthorized cooling of government premises. #JusticeServed #CloudsInContempt #LegalAbsurdity (satire)
igHook: Would you try to serve a subpoena to a thundercloud?
